text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected for enterprise customer 'Galileo' in eu-west-1 (dedicated pool rwpool-eu-3). p99=2300ms (SLO=1500ms). Triggered at 2026-03-15T02:13:54Z. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tenant-latency>.

elaine: ack, I'm on. Paging oncall @oncall-sre — please join. Any immediate customer impact?

oncall-sre: on it, joining now. Can someone post the quick metrics dumps (per-tenant p99, qps)?

raj: pulling metrics. Preliminary: overall pool p99 up, but Galileo tenant is driving 78% of tokens in the last 10m. Per-tenant p99: Galileo=2.3s, other_top_tenant=0.7s. QPS: Galileo burst ~420qps sustained for ~8m.

sam: checking model servers and KV cache stats. Seeing high KV miss rate for galileo prefixes, cache eviction climbs. Possibly large context prefixes causing cache churn.

kai: adding: scheduler shows increased batching for Galileo requests leading to higher latency tails. Likely large prompt sizes + no prefix KVC hit.

elain: (typo) sorry meant elaine: thanks. Can we isolate Galileo to dedicated circuit/eviction bucket to protect other tenants? We have tenant isolation playbook.

sam: yes — we can create a tenant traffic policy to route Galileo to a warm spare subset and cap concurrency. Proposed steps:
1) throttle Galileo token QPS to 250 (soft cap)
2) create an isolation traffic group and move new requests there
3) apply aggressive prefix caching policy (longer TTL) for Galileo if safe

elaine: do the throttle first. Command to run?

sam: run: ```curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/policies/tenants/galileo/throttle" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"token_qps":250,"mode":"soft"}'```

raj: running throttle now, executing from eu-control-1...

raj: response: 200 OK. Policy applied, request_id=msg-8f2a. Confirmed tokens QPS limit -> 250.

incident-bot: Incident note: policy change applied by raj.

kai: starting migration of new traffic to isolation group `galileo-isolate-1` (warm spare nodes). This will keep existing connections but route new sessions. Command: ```routingctl move-tenant --tenant galileo --group galileo-isolate-1 --mode gradual --rate 20%/m```

kai: kicked off at 02:19Z. Monitoring.

sam: also patching KV caching TTL for galileo prefixes now: ```adminctl cache set-ttl --tenant galileo --prefix "galileo:*" --ttl 1800s``` expecting to reduce misses.

sam: TTL update applied.

elaine: monitoring dashboards — please post p99/p95 in 2m. Also @amy-cs please ping Galileo account team and let them know we're actively mitigating; ask for any correlating customer-side changes.

amy-cs: pinged Galileo SRE (Liam) via the escalation channel. He replied: "we started a large batch export job ~02:05Z for analytics publishing across multiple endpoints, can try throttling it if needed." They will try to limit their export to reduce qps.

raj: 02:24Z metrics: pool p99 down to 1.1s, Galileo tenant p99 down to 1.9s and trending. QPS for Galileo down to 260 after throttle + customer action.

elaine: good. Keep monitoring. We need to evaluate whether to evict heavy requests or roll a temporary model variant with stricter token limits. Thoughts?

kai: eviction is heavier — if customer balks at throttling we can apply request-size cap: ```policyctl set-request-cap --tenant galileo --max_tokens 2048``` This prevents extremely long contexts driving batch times.

amy-cs: Galileo confirms they reduced export rate by 70% and will re-run smaller batches. They asked for ETA to fully restore prior latency.

oncall-sre: current ETA guess: if trend continues, 30-45m to return to baseline under current controls. We'll reassess in 10m.

sam: seeing a few anomalous error spikes (429s) during throttle ramp; redirecting new sessions to warm spare caused some connection throttles. I'm increasing warm spare capacity by adding 2 nodes in eu-west-1: ```infractl pool-scale --pool rwpool-eu-3-warm --add 2```

raj: scale started. Infra reported new nodes healthy at 02:33Z.

incident-bot: Reminder: page escalation for enterprise SLA if customer-visible SLO exceeds 60m. Current breach duration: ~20m.

elaine: document timeline in warroom doc and prepare a short customer-facing summary. Key points: cause = customer burst + cache churn; mitigations = throttle, isolation, cache TTL, warm spare scale. Next: post-mortem to follow with evaluation of automatic tenant-protection rules.

amy-cs: sending summary to Galileo: "We've applied a soft throttle and isolated new sessions; we've scaled warm spare capacity; your export job reduction helped. We expect p99 to be back under 1.5s within 30-45m. We'll keep you updated every 15m."

raj: 02:40Z metrics: p99 pool = 0.9s, Galileo p99=1.1s, errors <0.1%. Looks stable.

elaine: nice work. Can someone capture the exact commands and timeline in the incident doc? I'll be handing off to night shift in 30m — want a clean handoff note with follow-ups: (1) verify TTL persists for next deploy, (2) evaluate adding automatic tenant burst protection, (3) run a sim test for large exports in staging.

sam: I'll paste the command history into the doc now.

sam: paste: ```
# 02:17Z raj
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/policies/tenants/galileo/throttle" -d '{"token_qps":250,"mode":"soft"}'
# 02:19Z kai
routingctl move-tenant --tenant galileo --group galileo-isolate-1 --mode gradual --rate 20%/m
# 02:20Z sam
adminctl cache set-ttl --tenant galileo --prefix "galileo:*" --ttl 1800s
# 02:32Z sam
infractl pool-scale --pool rwpool-eu-3-warm --add 2
```

amy-cs: Galileo just replied: "Thanks, seeing improvements. We'll keep exports reduced for next hour. Please share post-mortem."

elaine: ok, I'm going to update the warroom doc and create a PM to schedule a follow-up post-mortem with SRE/infra/serving/product. Handoff in 20.

oncall-sre: taking 2hr handoff. I'll watch the dashboards and escalate if metrics regress. Add me to the incident doc as the on-call owner.

incident-bot: Note: incident status -> mitigated. Duration so far 32m. Severity: sev2 (customer SLO breach, service degraded for dedicated customer).

elaine: final note before handoff: root cause hypothesis = uncoordinated heavy customer export + prefix KV-cache TTL defaults + lack of auto-tenant-burst-protection. Action items: 1) post-mortem + timeline, 2) implement auto-throttle rule prototype, 3) test eviction vs request-cap policies in staging. I'll create tickets.

amy-cs: I'll schedule a customer follow-up call for tomorrow with Galileo account and SRE.

elaine: handing off now to @oncall-sre. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
